overview: The open-window packet is the state anchor for inventory anti-cheat: modern anticheats mirror the S2D open into a simulated window state and then validate every C0E click against it. Grim records the container id and type on the send side and rejects impossible click combinations, and its CompensatedInventory runs the full openWindowID state machine. Intave timestamps the open so its inventory-click-analysis check can measure click delay, and Artemis transaction-confirms the open to flip the inventory-open flag. Classic repos stop at wrappers (FlopAC WrappedOutOpenWindow, Kauri PacketHandler, Negativity PacketType).

checks.name: BadPacketsP invalid click (Grim)
checks.purpose: Reject crafted window-click packets whose button values are impossible for the click type.
checks.how_it_works: PacketSendListener records containerType and containerId from the S2D OPEN_WINDOW packet; PacketReceiveListener then validates every C0E click: button range per click type (PICKUP/QUICK_MOVE/CLONE 0-2, SWAP 0-8 or 40, THROW 0-1, QUICK_CRAFT a fixed set, PICKUP_ALL 0). The verbose line also reports whether the click's window id matches the container opened by S2D, and the packet is cancelled on repeated flags.
checks.detects: Crafted C0E packets used for packet-crash exploits and invalid-click lag machines, plus clicks that reference a window the server never opened.
checks.variations: CrashD in the same repo combines the S2D open with click parsing to drive crash checks; FlopAC WrappedOutOpenWindow and Kauri PacketHandler only wrap the packet.

checks.name: CompensatedInventory open-window state (Grim)
checks.purpose: Emulate the server-side inventory and open-window id so click, slot and item packets can be validated against client-visible state.
checks.how_it_works: On the S2D OPEN_WINDOW send it stores openWindowID from the container id (the horse-window variant is handled separately); the S2F set-slot and S30 window-items handlers then route updates to the player inventory (id 0) or the opened menu (id equal to openWindowID). Clicks against a mismatched window id are treated as invalid, and closeActiveInventory resets the menu, carried item and id.
checks.detects: Inventory desync, chest-stealer and inventory-manipulation that click windows the server never opened, and carried-item spoofing.
checks.variations: AbstractContainerMenu in the same repo replays valid click semantics on the emulated menu.

checks.name: Inventory click delay analysis (Intave)
checks.purpose: Flag chest-stealer and auto-inventory modules by measuring click timing and slot distance against the window open.
checks.how_it_works: The openWindowPacket subscription on outbound OPEN_WINDOW records lastWindowOpenTimestamp and marks the window open under tick feedback. The windowClickPacket subscription collects distance-time and slot-time samples per window; on close, if the sample count exceeds 30 it runs statistics (mean, variance, slope, Pearson correlation) and flags constant-speed item taking, excessive speed, and distance-indifferent patterns, nerfing the player's attack damage past 100 VL.
checks.detects: ChestStealer, inventory cleaners and refill modules that take items at uniform speed or ignore slot distance.
checks.variations: NotOpenCheck in the same package flags clicks when no window was opened; PacketEventDispatch.sentWindowOpen stores the slot count announced by S2D.

checks.name: WindowOpen wrapper and inventory-open flag (Artemis)
checks.purpose: Register the S2D packet and transaction-confirm the open so Artemis knows the player's inventory is open.
checks.how_it_works: GPacketPlayServerWindowOpen wraps PacketPlayOutOpenWindow with a readable buffer; EmulatorPreProcessor handles it by scheduling a transaction-confirmed PacketAction whose pre() stops item use and sets the inventory-open flag, so movement and click checks can distinguish windowed from normal play at the right tick.
checks.detects: Chest-stealer and window-state desync where clicks or movement are processed against a stale inventory state.
checks.variations: PacketExecutor registers the wrapper; PacketPlayServerWindowOpen is the API interface. Kauri (funkemunky-KauriV3) PacketHandler sets inventoryOpen(true) and resets lastInventoryOpen on a keepalive-confirmed OPEN_WINDOW.
